description: Almenara is a team of curious computer science students focused on extracting insights from complex data. We enjoy exploring different approaches to analyze and interpret, turning raw information into meaningful knowledge.
summary:
We built Almenara, an interactive platform that combines NASA FIRMS observations from MODIS and VIIRS into a comparable fire history across four study regions. The sensors detect hotspots at different resolutions, so a change in instruments can look like a change in fire activity. Almenara aligns both records on a common grid, calibrates them across sensors, and estimates sampled fire radiative energy. Its maps and calendars distinguish observations, reconstructed values, and gaps in coverage.

For our primary users, researchers and land managers, we built Fire Copilot, a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant. It draws on satellite records and cites scientific sources to help users investigate past events, compare fire seasons, and verify the evidence behind its answers.

For emergency services and firefighters, we implemented a classical machine learning model that runs offline. It estimates the likelihood of elevated satellite-detectable thermal activity in a selected area over the next 24 hours, 7 days, and 14 days, and shows which factors drive each estimate. This gives teams an additional signal for preparedness and helps them prioritize where to monitor.
details:
ALMENARA — FIRMS Harmonizer is an interactive platform that helps people compare satellite fire activity across instruments, places, and decades. A rise in reported hotspots can reflect more fire activity, a more sensitive instrument, or better observation coverage. ALMENARA brings those factors into the same analysis so users can investigate whether a pattern persists after harmonization. Our current implementation covers four study areas from 2000 to 2026: Chilecito and La Rioja in Argentina, the Iberian Peninsula, Orlando and central Florida, and Manaus and the surrounding Amazonas region. The local analysis cube contains more than 729,000 grid-cell days derived from real NASA FIRMS observations. Coverage varies by date, sensor, and location.

From satellite detections to comparable measurements. We combine MODIS observations from Terra and Aqua with VIIRS observations from Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21. The processing pipeline removes duplicate detections, accounts for the widening of MODIS footprints away from nadir, and places measurements on a common H3 hexagonal grid. Empirical quantile mapping adjusts for differences in the instruments’ fire radiative power distributions and detection thresholds. We combine readings within each cell and use an explicit one-hour integration assumption to estimate sampled fire radiative energy. Regional totals use each cell’s actual area. Persistent thermal signatures and published gas-flare locations help users screen industrial heat sources while preserving access to the underlying observations.

An interactive record users can inspect and challenge. Users can select a study area or draw their own, choose an exact day or a longer date range, and compare raw detections with calibrated energy. The observations table lets users trace a result back to daily detection counts, reported power, and contributing sensors, then export the record as CSV. A synchronized map, calendar, and seasonal charts show where activity concentrates and how its timing changes. The calendar distinguishes reported activity, observed zeros supported by satellite coverage, reconstructed values, and unknown days. The impact view estimates dry biomass consumed and, where measured annual land cover and supported fuel factors are available, primary PM₂.₅ emissions.

Validation and forecasting. Our Chaos Monkey tool deliberately withholds satellite observations and compares a Kalman reconstruction with the intact input record. The audit also measures the difference between pre- and post-2012 distributions and compares annual indicators with the independently derived MODIS MCD64A1 burned-area product where monthly inventories are complete. In the latest documented audit, harmonization reduced cross-era divergence by approximately 43% to 87% across the four regions. Three met the predefined Chow-test criterion after harmonization, and none reached the 88% divergence-reduction target. Orlando’s remaining discontinuity is visible in the audit.

The application offers two distinct forecasts. A fire radiative energy forecast is shown only when observation coverage and held-out tests support it. Risk AI estimates the probability of satellite-observable thermal events over 24 hours, 7 days, and 14 days. It uses information available through the date selected by the user and shows the influence of seasonal history, longer-term trends, and recent heat. These probabilities describe thermal signals. Confirming an ignition or an industrial accident requires independent incident records.

Technology and intended impact. We built the scientific pipeline in Python with NumPy and SciPy, the local data layer with DuckDB, PyArrow, Parquet, and H3, and the API with FastAPI. The browser interface uses TypeScript, React, deck.gl, MapLibre, and Canvas. A prepared installation runs offline on a standard computer, and the public demo is packaged with Docker for Google Cloud Run. Fire Copilot answers questions about the selected place and dates using local archive calculations by default. Optional online research adds sourced context, while the scientific quantities come from the same Python and DuckDB calculations used by the dashboard. The team used AI-assisted development and reviewed the resulting work through tests and verification reports.

We designed ALMENARA for researchers comparing fire seasons, land managers investigating recurring activity, and civil-protection analysts deciding which signals warrant further investigation. Its intended impact is to make long-term fire analysis more comparable and easier to audit, especially where sensor changes, missing observations, and limited connectivity would otherwise make the evidence difficult to interpret.

The public github repo is here:
https://github.com/AdamBourbahh/Almenara
